name: WordCraft
tagline: A free, open-source word processor that works like Microsoft Word - runs on your computer, no subscription, no account.
sentence: Open a document, format it with styles, tables and track changes the same way you would in Word, but without paying Microsoft $7-13 a month.

visual.alt: WordCraft editing 'The Open Studio Handbook': Navigation pane with headings on the left, a Word-style ribbon toolbar with Home tab, Styles gallery, and formatted text with bold, italic and blue headings.
visual.caption: The editor with a formatted document, showing the ribbon toolbar and navigation pane - the same layout as Microsoft Word.

board.say: You need to write and format documents - styles, tables, track changes, references - but Word costs $7-13 a month and the free alternatives use a different interface.
board.eg: You want to open a .docx file from a colleague, review it with tracked changes, update the table of contents, and send it back as a PDF.

board.say: You open WordCraft on your computer, or an AI agent opens it through its built-in command interface.
board.eg: Double-click the app, or connect it to Claude Code - WordCraft has over 400 commands an agent can call.

board.say: Your document files: .docx, .odt, .rtf, .html, Markdown, LaTeX and plain text - including Word's own files with their formatting intact.
board.eg: Open a .docx proposal from a client and keep the styles, headers and tracked changes.

board.say: It gives you a full Word-style workspace with a ribbon toolbar, styles, tables and review tools, all running locally.
steps: Format text with the ribbon: fonts, styles, headings, lists, the same shortcuts Word uses (Ctrl+B for bold, F4 to repeat)
Build tables with merged cells, banded rows and sorting; add headers, footers, columns and page numbers
Review with track changes, comments, spelling and grammar checking in 21 languages, and compare two documents side by side
Save as .docx, PDF (with selectable text and bookmarks), .odt, .rtf, Markdown, LaTeX or plain text
board.eg: The README demo: open the sample document, apply heading styles, insert a table of contents, and export to PDF.

board.say: A formatted document saved on your own computer, in the format you need.

outputs.eg: A Word file you can hand back to a colleague - styles, tracked changes and comments preserved
A finished PDF with selectable text, clickable links and bookmarks, ready to send
The same ribbon-and-styles workflow Word charges $7-13/month for, running on your machine for free

before: Writing and formatting documents with styles, tables and tracked changes means paying Microsoft $7-13 a month - or learning a free tool that looks and works differently.
Opening a colleague's .docx file with all its formatting means owning Word, or hoping a converter keeps everything intact.
after: The same ribbon-and-styles workflow, on your own computer, for free - with the keyboard shortcuts Word users already know.
Open .docx files with formatting intact, review with tracked changes, and export to PDF or send back as .docx.
uses_note: WordCraft went public on October 7, 2026. It is 9 days old and in alpha, so named real-world use is still very early.

steps: [Download WordCraft](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases) for your computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) and install it.
Launch a sample with `wordcraft --sample` and test the basics: apply a heading style, insert a table, and add a tracked change.
If you have a .docx file from Word, drag it in and check that styles, headers and tracked changes come through. Export it to PDF.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft

If that scan passes: download and install WordCraft, open a sample document with `wordcraft --sample`, apply heading styles, insert a table of contents, and export to PDF. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: About 86 MB (the Linux AppImage is 86.1 MB; Mac and Windows installers are in the same range). Source builds require Rust 1.90+.
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses a GPU compositor (Metal, Vulkan or DirectX 12) and falls back to all CPU cores without a GPU. Re-layout of a 188-page document takes about 1.4 ms.
footprint.runs_on: Mac (universal - Apple silicon and Intel), Windows (x64, arm64, x86), Linux (x86_64, aarch64), FreeBSD (x86_64) and the web (via WebAssembly). Installers: DMG, MSI, AppImage, Flatpak, DEB, RPM.

best_for: You know Word's ribbon-and-styles workflow and want a free alternative that works the same way - styles, tracked changes, the same shortcuts
You want an AI agent to create and edit .docx files and PDFs through a command interface, without needing a Word license
skip_if: You need a reliable word processor for contracts, CVs or client work today - this is in early alpha, and commenters report crashes and freezes
You depend on .docx round-trip fidelity (charts, SmartArt, exact pagination) - those are not fully working yet

alternatives.name: LibreOffice Writer
alternatives.line: The established free word processor. More stable and complete, but a different interface - not a Word look-alike.

alternatives.name: OnlyOffice
alternatives.line: A free office suite with a Word-style ribbon. Closer to Word's look, with better .docx fidelity than most free editors.

alternatives.name: Google Docs
alternatives.line: Free and browser-based. Handles basic .docx files, but needs an internet connection and stores documents in the cloud.

watch: **Early alpha - not ready for professional work.** The Hacker News thread (101 points, 108 comments) includes reports of crashes on an M4 MacBook when changing text to a heading. One guide says: keep WordCraft for drafts, use a mature editor for a CV, a contract or a thesis.

**Another storytold pick after last week's five.** WordCraft is the sixth ArtCraft/storytold tool in two weeks. That concentration reflects a real moment - Microsoft Office replacements launched alongside the Adobe ones - but one org's fate now affects a large share of recent editions.

**Built by a very small team using AI.** Trendshift shows 2 contributors and 735 commits. The same pattern as PhotoCraft: one developer with a heavy AI assist. Long-term maintenance is an open question.

**.docx fidelity is untested on real-world files.** The project's own beta requirements include testing against a corpus of real documents. Charts and SmartArt do not survive a round trip, and pagination does not yet match Word exactly.
